question: On locally-hosted deterministic SPAs, does any state representation achieve predictive PMI beyond what action labels alone determine? Specifically: (1) what PMI does an action-label baseline MI(S_next; A) achieve, (2) does DOM or network representation exceed it, and (3) does conditional mutual information MI(S_next; DOM | A) indicate DOM encodes predictive state variation not already captured by the action label?
hypothesis: Action-label PMI MI(S_next; A) dominates on deterministic SPAs where next state is fully determined by current state and action. DOM-feature PMI MI(S_next; DOM) does not exceed action-label PMI, and conditional mutual information MI(S_next; DOM | A) is negligible (near zero). This is because deterministic server logic makes action labels a sufficient statistic for next-state prediction — DOM features merely recover the FSM state label that action labels already encode. Network-request PMI is zero (inherited from prior experiments). Therefore, no representation achieves predictive structure 'beyond memory' on these deterministic SPAs, and C-WEB-DYNAMICS 'predictive dynamical structure beyond memory and ordinary similarity' is not supported in this setting.
falsifier: DOM features exceed action-label PMI on >= 1/3 tested SPAs (MI(S_next; DOM) > MI(S_next; A) by >= 0.05 bits with permutation p < 0.0167 after Bonferroni correction for 3 comparisons), OR conditional mutual information MI(S_next; DOM | A) is substantial (> 0.1 bits) on >= 1/3 SPAs, OR the synthetic positive control with genuine environmental dynamics fails to show MI(S_next; DOM | A) > 0.1 bits, OR the null control (shuffled action labels) produces false-positive DOM contribution > 0.05 bits.
baselines: Action-label PMI MI(S_next; A) — primary baseline, represents the deterministic FSM's action-to-state mapping (action type: click/fill/submit/navigate)
URL-only PMI (trivial zero on single-path SPAs — structural, not empirical, inherited from prior experiments)

Network-request PMI from parent experiments (request-side: dashboard 0.881 tautological, multistep 0.0, wizard 0.0; response-side: dashboard 0.034, multistep 0.0, wizard 0.0 — inherited, not re-measured)
Frequency baseline P(S_next) — marginal next-state distribution, expected accuracy 1/|S|
positive_control: Synthetic SPA with 8 states, 4 actions, AND an independent environmental counter that increments every transition regardless of action. DOM features encode both action-determined state AND counter value. Expected: MI(S_next; DOM | A) > 0.1 bits because DOM contains counter information not in action label. This verifies the pipeline can detect genuine environmental dynamics when present.
null_control: Shuffled action labels on real SPA data (dashboard, multistep_form, wizard). Action labels permuted within trajectories preserving trajectory structure. Expected: MI(S_next; DOM | A_shuffled) should not be significantly > 0 (permutation p > 0.0167 after Bonferroni correction for 3 comparisons). This verifies no false-positive environmental dynamics detection.
measurement_validity: Same 3 locally-hosted SPAs as parent experiments (dashboard port 3849, multistep_form port 3848, wizard port 3850) to enable direct comparison

Reuse existing raw_dom_captures.json from EXP-PHYSICS-34719136202 (804 transitions, sha256 85efd4675f1fcbe841200cbd406338f1b81aaf923e9f2005982f92ee24a7d7a1) — no new data collection needed for DOM features
Action labels extracted from trajectory data: action_type (click/fill/submit/navigate) without target element identity
Same PMI computation framework as parent (alpha=1.0 smoothing, 80/20 temporal split, 1000 permutations, Bonferroni correction for 3 comparisons)
DOM state representation: visible_text_hash (SHA-16 of document.body.innerText) from parent experiment — the only DOM feature that showed variation
Deterministic random seed (seed=42) for reproducibility; Python HASHSEED=0
Synthetic positive control captures new data with independent environmental counter
n_test >= 30 per site required (same as parent: dashboard 40, multistep 40, wizard 31)
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) action-label PMI MI(S_next; A) >= DOM PMI MI(S_next; DOM) on >= 2/3 sites (i.e., action labels dominate or equal DOM); (2) conditional MI MI(S_next; DOM | A) < 0.1 bits on >= 2/3 sites (DOM adds negligible predictive power beyond action); (3) positive control passes (synthetic MI(S_next; DOM | A) > 0.1 bits with permutation p < 0.0167); (4) null control passes (shuffled MI(S_next; DOM | A_shuffled) permutation p > 0.0167); (5) data sufficiency met (n_test >= 30 per site); (6) no pipeline errors — verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING for C-WEB-DYNAMICS in deterministic SPA setting (action-label dominance confirms tautology, no predictive dynamics beyond memory). If DOM exceeds action-label PMI on >= 1/3 sites, OR MI(S_next; DOM | A) > 0.1 bits on >= 1/3 sites, verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. If controls fail or data insufficient, verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: If DOM exceeds action-label PMI or MI(S_next; DOM | A) is substantial, demonstrates that rendered-page features encode predictive state variation beyond what action labels capture — even on deterministic servers. Would justify DOM integration into SPIDER observation layer as non-trivial physics. Would indicate session-state or hidden server dynamics not captured by action labels.
product_consequence_negative: If action labels dominate and DOM adds nothing beyond them, confirms that DOM PMI on deterministic SPAs is tautological FSM state recovery, not predictive dynamics. C-WEB-DYNAMICS 'beyond memory' is not supported in this setting. DOM integration as physics is not warranted. Physics lane must investigate production SPAs with non-deterministic rendering where action labels may not be sufficient statistics.
estimated_cost: Very low: reuse existing raw_dom_captures.json from parent experiment; compute action-label PMI and conditional MI offline; synthetic positive control requires small new data capture (~50 transitions); no model calls. ~850 transitions total, 1000 permutations per site, 4 mutual information computations per site.
expected_information_gain: High: directly resolves audit B4 (missing history/memory baseline) and the identifiability question (is DOM PMI just FSM state recovery?). A negative result (action-label dominance) cleanly falsifies C-WEB-DYNAMICS on deterministic SPAs and redirects Physics to production SPAs. A positive result (DOM exceeds action-label) would be a genuine surprise indicating hidden session dynamics. Either outcome changes the claim/product decision.
